content:
The image shows leaves covered with a white, powdery coating across the leaf surface. The underlying leaf tissue is green but heavily coated with what appears to be a dense white powdery layer. This is the hallmark symptom of Powdery Mildew.

Key visual evidence:
- Dense white powdery growth covering the leaf surface
- Green leaf tissue visible beneath the coating
- The powdery texture and white coloration match the description of white powdery sporulation expanding and converging to cover entire leaves

This does not match Gray Mold (which produces gray-brown spore masses), Late Blight (water-soaked brown lesions with fuzzy sporulation on undersides), or Leaf Mold (olive-green velvety mold on undersides).
